merger_name: Woolworths - supermarket site in Lakeview Street, Mariginiup WA
merger_description:
Woolworths Group Limited (**Woolworths**), via its subsidiary, Fabcot Pty Ltd (**Fabcot**), proposes to acquire a freehold interest in 38 Lakeview Street, Mariginiup, Western Australia (the **Target Site**) (the **Acquisition**). The Target Site is located in a mixed urban development / rural area, is currently used as a residential dwelling, and is approximately 8.22 hectares in size.

Woolworths proposes to construct a new shopping centre at the Target Site, anchored by a full-line Woolworths supermarket, which is anticipated to open in July 2032.

Woolworths is an ASX-listed retailer operating a national supermarket network, including full-line Woolworths supermarkets, Woolworths Metro outlets and online grocery services, together with other retail and consumer businesses.

Fabcot acquires and develops non-residential property for the Woolworths Group’s retail network.

Lakewood Estate Development (No 1) Pty Ltd is a special purpose vehicle created for the purpose of development of the Target Site.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application had
regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. Woolworths proposes to open a new supermarket in
Mariginiup, WA, with the closest existing Woolworths
supermarket located more than 6km away from the Target
Site
b. there are alternative grocery retailers in and around the
surrounding local area, including Coles, ALDI, IGA and
Farmer Jack’s
c. the Target Site is not currently used for grocery retailing.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds determined under section 51ABP(1) being met. The ACCC
observes that the targeted notification requirements for
supermarkets determined under section 51ABQ(1) may also apply,
but it does not consider it necessary to reach a concluded view in
this regard.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
